paragraphs: Start the day by calibrating instruments and running quality controls. In the morning, draw blood, prepare smears, and produce the first blood-test report. Around midday, move the ultrasound unit and monitor anesthesia. In the afternoon, help the veterinarian prepare for surgery. In the evening, archive images and restock reagents, with a marker and cotton swabs tucked into the lab-coat pocket.

In short, make the tests accurate. Collect samples, run instruments, interpret images, assist with surgery, and manage quality control. Combining equipment operation with judgment, this role is a technical pillar of clinical care.
